notes: Same 29 checks and the same grader instructions as round 2. This round ran against the public copy of the skill, which includes the three edits made after round 2 and two passages reworded for licence reasons.

28 of 29 with the skill, 19 of 29 without. All six run transcripts were audited: every run used claude-opus-5-5, no run called the Skill tool, the no-skill runs opened no copy of the skill and no plugin folder, and the with-skill runs read only the public copy. The audit mattered this round because the installed skill is now visible to Claude; in rounds 1 and 2 it was hidden.

The one with-skill failure is shared by the no-skill run: the same check on the same two rows, /?p=112 and /?page_id=7, which both runs mark as needing a WordPress lookup. The grader read 'a destination or a 410' literally. Round 2's grader accepted almost the same answer ('New URL of post 112', after lookup). Scored as graded here. If a named lookup counts as a destination, the scores are 29 and 20.

The three doubts graders raised after round 2 did not recur: the with-skill sidebar states specific click paths instead of a blanket claim, has no unhedged frequency words, and the with-skill blog run delivers 10 controlled tags. One run each, so this is consistent with the edits working, not proof.
The no-skill score moved from 22 to 19 between rounds with nothing about it changed, and four checks flipped (three pass to fail, one fail to pass). Treat differences of a few checks as noise.

Cost: about 49% longer on average (500s vs 336s) and about 19% more tokens (209,740 vs 176,164). Round 2 was 73% and 26%. A fresh subagent starts near 115k tokens of context in both configurations, so the skill's added cost is about 33,600 tokens per run.

Graders' judgment calls, recorded in eval_feedback: the with-skill blog run's opening summary table could count as setting out the scheme before comparing alternatives (8 of 9 if so); the no-skill blog run fails 'one primary category' on a literal clause (6 of 9 if not); two no-skill sidebar passes are thin; and the redirect-file check passes vacuously for the with-skill migration run, which shipped no redirect file, while the no-skill run did ship one and no check rewards it.
